newsitem.title: USA: No ruling yet in Jacksonville, Fla. tobacco case.
newsitem.headline: No ruling yet in Jacksonville, Fla. tobacco case.

text.p: A Jacksonville judge did not rule Wednesday on whether to postpone a product liability case against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, brought by anti-smoking attorney Norwood "Woody" Wilner, the judge's secretary said.
Circuit Judge Michael Weatherby also gave no ruling on whether Wilner could seek punitive damages against Reynolds on behalf of his client, Joann Karbiwnyk, the secretary said.
It was not clear whether the judge would rule before the Independence Day holiday July 4.
Weatherby heard arguments from Wilner and from attorneys for Reynolds at a pre-trial hearing Tuesday on both issues.
Karbiwnyk, 58, says her smoking of Reynolds' Winston and Salem brands caused her to develop lung cancer diagnosed in 1995.
Weatherby ruled last week he would not postpone the case, set for trial Aug 4. However attorneys for Reynolds made a renewed plea Tuesday for a delay till October, saying they were not ready yet.
